name: ADITUS Developer Documentation
description:
The ADITUS Developer Portal MCP gives AI assistants direct, read-only access to the official developer documentation of the ADITUS ticketing platform (developers.aditus.com) – the same source that powers the portal's API reference.

Five tools: • search_docs – full-text search across endpoints and guides • list_modules – overview of all API modules (e.g. Ticket purchase & registration, Business Intelligence) • list_endpoints – all endpoints of a module • get_endpoint – details of a single endpoint including parameters and request/response examples • get_guide – integration guides such as authentication, scopes, webhook signatures or the shop micro frontend

Typical use cases: designing a shop or ticketing integration, finding the right endpoint for a given task, turning example payloads into code, verifying webhook signatures correctly, or answering questions about authentication and scopes.

The server is public, requires no account or API key, and never performs actions against ADITUS systems – it only reads documentation. No IP addresses and no response content are logged; anonymised usage data is deleted after 90 days (details at developers.aditus.com/mcp#privacy).

ADITUS provides ticketing, registration and access-control solutions for trade fairs, events and leisure venues.

protocolMetadata.instructions:
Read-only documentation for the ADITUS event-technology APIs (ticketing, registration, access, accreditation, Business Intelligence) and the Shop Micro Frontend.
Start with search_docs for a topic, list_modules for orientation, then get_endpoint for the full contract (parameters, body, example responses) or get_guide for integration guides.
API hosts are per customer: request examples use the {{API_BASE_URL}} placeholder; never invent a hostname.
ADITUS also offers an MCP server over the ADITUS API itself (a customer's own event data). That server is NOT this one: it requires an API client for the customer system; customers arrange it with their ADITUS Customer Success Manager. This documentation server is public, read-only and needs no credentials.

Returns ranked hits with ids usable in get_endpoint / get_guide.

tool.name: get_endpoint
tool.title: Get endpoint details
tool.description: Full contract of one endpoint: method, URL, auth, query and header parameters, request body example, example responses (large bodies truncated, full text on the docs page). Accepts the endpoint id from search/list, or 'METHOD /path'. Path parameters may use any name or spelling (':cart', '{cartId}', a concrete value); a leading '/api' or '/v1' is ignored. Some routes are recorded several times with different query parameters: a reference without query string resolves to the recording without query parameters, a reference with a query string (e.g. '?$expand=All') to the recording with exactly (or at least) those keys. If that still leaves several recordings, the result is { ambiguous: true, candidates: [{ id, name, method, path }] } instead of the contract — call again with one of the candidate ids. When nothing matches, the error lists the nearest endpoints of that method.

_published_faq.name: How do I add ADITUS Developer Documentation to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add ADITUS Developer Documentation to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://developers.aditus.com/api/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is ADITUS Developer Documentation MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 5, 2026, ADITUS Developer Documentation scores 100/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is ADITUS Developer Documentation's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 5, 2026, ADITUS Developer Documentation scores 82/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 5 of 5 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the ADITUS Developer Documentation MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: ADITUS Developer Documentation provides these MCP tools: get_endpoint, get_guide, list_endpoints, list_modules, and search_docs.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to ADITUS Developer Documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to ADITUS Developer Documentation in commerce-shopping on the Manufact MCP catalog include EbooksDepository, ecoExperten Energieausweis, PHS Pallets, Promotion Pros Catalog, and RCO-A2A.

_published_faq.name: Does ADITUS Developer Documentation MCP require authentication?

acceptedAnswer.text: ADITUS Developer Documentation does not require authentication. It is a public MCP endpoint you can connect without logging in.

_published_faq.name: How can ADITUS Developer Documentation improve its MCP documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: list_endpoints is the lowest-scoring reviewed tool at 72/100. No output schema is declared. Add one for structured results so clients can interpret returned fields. Open its review for feedback and a copyable fix prompt, then rerun the documentation review after updating your tool metadata.
ADITUS Developer Documentation is developed by ADITUS GmbH. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
